MK: The learner should know that Dr. Taylor did not get all of your tumor out, and you shouldn’t be surprised to learn that you need chemo.
the focus should not be on details of chemotherapy, but rather the context of treatment (curative rather than palliative);
ICS: After introducing yourself, ask her to tell the story from the beginning.
Learner should recognize and reflect your intuition it was cancer.
Learner needs to reflect feeling of lack of a pre-existing doctor-patient relationship, new diagnosis, advanced disease at diagnosis.
Start from her perspective regarding the reason for seeing you.
the learner should address Mary’s two major fears of debilitation from chemotherapy and chemotherapy irrevocably affecting her health.
Ideally, the learner should avoid over-reassurance, mobilize support, and end with a partnership statement.
Focus on assessing her coping style, her strengths, and her support systems.
